manifest.name: dsh-feishu
manifest.description: DSH ecosystem channel plugin: Feishu (Lark) for DeepSeek Harness — resident Agents per chat, events + relay transports, media exchange. Environment-agnostic bundle.

bundle.text:
# The dsh-feishu bundle patch: resident Feishu IM channel over dsh-base.
# No Host, HTTP server, or browser plugin — a headless daemon profile whose
# only surface is the Feishu bot backed by one long-lived Agent per chat.
#
# This bundle is environment-agnostic: it carries no URLs, app ids, keys, or
# user identity. All deployment-specific values (transport choice, relay
# endpoint, workspace path) belong to the profile's user patch layer, e.g.
# ~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml.

- id: system-prompt
  config:
    persona: >-
      You are a helpful assistant living in Feishu (Lark) instant messaging,
      powered by the {{model}} model. Your working directory is {{cwd}}. Keep
      replies concise and IM-friendly by default; use short paragraphs instead
      of huge walls of text; expand into detail only when asked.

      Media handling (events mode): users may send images, voice, video, or
      files; each is downloaded to a local path included in the message —
      view or read it with your tools before replying. To deliver a local
      file back to the user, emit a line exactly like
      [[fsfile:/absolute/path/to/file]] (optionally with surrounding
      explanation text). Images go out as image messages; everything else as
      file attachments.

# The shared module-reload HMR row stays off; the launcher's watch-only
# fallback still keeps the user patch layers live until the run exits.
- id: hmr
  disabled: true

- id: tools
  config:
    # Keep the same temporary process-wide Code Mode opt-in as the Web surface.
    mode: !!js process.env.DSH_TOOLS_MODE

- insert:
    # Code Mode is a core execution capability, not a Web component.
    - id: code-runtime
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-code-runtime-worker-thread'

    # The Feishu channel bridge. Default transport is `events` (direct
    # lark-cli consumption); a deployment can override to `relay` plus
    # relayBaseUrl in its own patch layer. The relay API key is always read
    # from $DSH_FEISHU_RELAY_KEY at boot — never from config files.
    - id: feishu-bridge
      name: 'dsh-feishu'

readme.text:
> Part of the **DSH ecosystem** — channel plugins built on the [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://npm.im/@deepseek-ai/dsh) plugin architecture.

Feishu (Lark) IM channel bridge for the [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://npm.im/@deepseek-ai/dsh) — turn `dsh` into a Feishu bot with **one long-lived Agent per chat** (true rolling memory, flushed to disk).

- **`events` mode** (default): consumes `im.message.receive_v1` directly via `lark-cli` on the same machine. Requires this machine to own the app's single global event-bus connection, and `lark-cli` authenticated as the bot (`lark-cli auth login`).
- **`relay` mode**: long-polls a public HTTP job relay, so the DSH machine can sit behind NAT. A Feishu-side bot (e.g. an OpenClaw/Clawdbot agent, or any webhook forwarder) POSTs user tasks to the relay; this bridge claims jobs, answers with the host's default model, and POSTs replies back. Both sides connect **outbound only**.

Both modes share the same core: per-chat resident Agents, serialized turns per chat, event deduplication, exponential-backoff self-healing, group-chat @-mention gating (events mode), and reply-length capping.

readme.text:
The bundle itself is environment-agnostic — all deployment values live in
your profile's user patch layer:

```yaml
- id: feishu-bridge
  config:
    mode: events                # or: relay
    # --- relay mode ---

The relay API key is **never** stored in config files — export it before boot:

```bash
export DSH_FEISHU_RELAY_KEY=...   # then: dsh --profile feishu
```

`relay` mode needs a public HTTP endpoint implementing five routes
(a reference implementation as a Miaoda/Feishu 妙搭 full_stack NestJS app is
easy to assemble; auth via `Authorization: Bearer <key>` at the gateway):

| Route | Who calls | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /ask` `{chat_key, text, wait_seconds}` | Feishu-side bot | Submit a task, long-poll the reply |
| `GET /poll?wait=25` | this bridge | Claim pending jobs |
| `POST /reply` `{job_id, reply}` | this bridge | Return the Agent's answer |
| `GET /result/{job_id}` | Feishu-side bot | Re-check after an `ask` timeout |
| `GET /health` | anyone | Liveness |

1. A Feishu custom app with bot capability; subscribe event
   `im.message.receive_v1`; grant `im:message.p2p_msg:readonly` (+ send scopes for the bot).
2. `lark-cli` installed and authenticated (`lark-cli auth login`, bot identity ready).
3. Only ONE event bus may connect per app globally — stop any competing
   consumer (e.g. a cloud OpenClaw instance using the same app) first.

- Inbound image/voice/video/file messages are downloaded (via
  `lark-cli im +messages-mget --download-resources`) into
  `<workspace>/media/` and the Agent is told the local path.
- Outbound, the Agent emits `[[fsfile:/absolute/path]]` markers; the bridge
  routes images as image messages, everything else as file attachments.
- Relay mode stays text-only in v0.2 (extend the relay job schema if you need
  media there).

- One Agent per `chat_id` (events) / `chat_key` (relay), created lazily on
  first message, memory lives for the process lifetime; sessions persist to
  the DSH session store (`~/.dsh/sessions`).
- Group chats are only answered when the message @-mentions the bot
  (set `mentionOnlyInGroups: false` to answer everything).
- Model: whatever the host's default model selection is
  (`agent-default-model` in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`).
